$$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
examples.problem:
Suppose that a $3 \times 3$ matrix $F$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1, \qquad
	R_3:=R_3+2R_1
$$

Given that $F$ has the LU factorization $F=LU,$ then $L=$
examples.worked_solution:
Applying $R_2:=R_2 + {\color{red}1} \cdot R_1$ and then $R_3:=R_3+ {\color{red}2} \cdot R_1$ is equivalent to multiplying $F$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062432/assets/5eb696ca679a0079e8460d472b6f172df4f2e29f5dfef6cbdee388c55dcb1db5.png)

Now, since $E_2E_1F=U,$ we can invert $E_2$ and $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}F & =U \\ {E}_{1}F & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ F & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ F & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ F & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ F & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 12 & 16 & -5\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 12 & 16 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =U.\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$
